column1: # adversarial audit (2026-07-30) of the cross-POS 'same' verdicts in
# lemma.equivalences.seed.tsv - the mutation-pair and unclassified families,
# 202 pairs; the s'-comparative, n'-verbal and suffix-variant families were
# not audited (structurally derivational, lower risk). Each pair was read
# against the printed entries in cregeen-nvh. refute = two lexemes conflated
# (the verdict in the seed is flipped to distinct); unsure = the print does
# not settle it. 77 refuted, 4 unsure, 121 confirmed.

column4: evidence

aarkey.n is 'yn aarkey' the sea (family F-8, radical faarkey s.m. 'the sea, billow'), but faarkey.v is the separate verb family F-7 'to bathe' (dy aarkey); Cregeen prints sea-noun and bathe-verb as distinct lexemes.

aill.n's bare-headword entry (A-54) is aill 'wish/pleasure' (family saillym 'I please', baill 'would wish', cha naill 'not wish'); faill.v spans faill 'fail' (F-22, daill 'did fail') and faill 'hire, engage for wages' (F-23), and only the subsidiary 'e aill: his hire, wages' entry belongs with faill.
dy arkiaght "to wait" (F-41, etym. from farkiaght) and farkiaght, printed variant of farkiaghey "waiting" (F-41), are the same wait verb with f dropped after dy.

Printed arrit is the participle of arr in both arr families ('offered', pt. of arr 'offer' A-100 with derivedFrom arr, and a bare pt. under arr 'shift' A-101), so arrit names a paradigm form of the arr verb entry(ies) that arr.v covers.

baart.n is "nyn baart" (your part), eclipsis of the NOUN paart "some, part" (P-6, proper target paart.n), while paart.x is the "cha baart" verb entry "would not part" belonging to the verb paartail/phaart "part, depart" (P-5).
beyr is Cregeen's printed spelling variant of bayr 'a way, avenue, lane' (both B-61, variant relation, yn veyr 'the lane, way, or avenue').

be.v is the copula family B-65 (dy ve 'to be', er ve 'hath been', bee 'will be'); bey.x is the separate B-64 be/bey printed with dy-be 'for cause, because' and erbey 'because, lit. on cause' - the 'cause' element, not the verb 'to be'.
bee'm "I will be" and my vee'm "if I be" (both family B-65) are 1sg forms of the one verb 'to be', vee'm being the lenited form under my.
bee v. 'be, will be' and row p. 'wast thou' (with emphatic rows) are both family B-65, row being the dependent past of the substantive verb 'be'.

beg a. "little, small" (B-76) and the veg pro. entry printed inside the same B-76 family, which Cregeen glosses as the lenited veg "ALSO understood to mean none or nothing" (cha daag eh veg dou), i.e. an extended use of the same word.

berr is 'overtake' (B-86), but the verr.v id is the printed verr 'will give, put, send, bring' (C-397, future of cur; its forms verr/verrym/verryms match that entry), while the 'did overtake' verr entry feeds berr.v.
Both family B-116: bishee is 'used for the verb bish, increase, augment, establish' and bishaghey is the verbal noun of the same increase verb.

blass.n is the noun entry "taste, savour, flavour" (s.m.), while blayst.v is the verb family (self form vlayst "did taste", preterite of the separate blass v. entry, id blass-2); noun entry conflated with the verb entry.
Both printed blayst entries are bare variant cross-references to blass ('taste, savour, flavour' s.m. and its verb) in the same family B-124.
boayrd s. m. "a table, a board" and buird a. d. "of a table or tables" is its genitive/attributive case form, both family B-153.

bolg.v is the verb 'roast, or raise blisters by fire' (B-166), but volg.n is a noun: 'yn volg' the belly (B-166, radical bolg.n) or the milt (M-121); roast-verb and belly/milt-noun are different lexemes.

boult.v is the bolt verb (B-189, voult 'did bolt'); voult.n keys the M-section entry 'yn voult: the mutton' (M-115, lenited mohlt 'a mutton') - the B-section 'yn voult: the bolt' already belongs to boult.n - so bolt vs mutton.
vra "(from bra) ever, used in poetry" (bra.n) and braa, printed variant of bra "ever, a contraction of bragh" (both B-202), gloss the same adverb 'ever'.

breg s.f. 'a lie' (B-218, = breag) and breig v. 'coax, endeavour to persuade' (B-229) are separate families with different meanings; a noun 'lie' and a verb 'coax' are distinct lexemes despite the shared root.
buitch.v is buitçh v. "bewitch(ing)" (B-272), while wuitch.n is wuitçh s. "witch", the mutated form of the NOUN buitçh s. f. "a witch" (proper target buitch.n).

Both are the copula: by is its past/conditional (the printed by entry B-294 is pos-less with no rival sense) and she the present (printed in the be-family B-65 as the affirmative answer); lemma-paradigms.nvh adopts by as a form of she.v.
caashey s.m. 'cheese' and e chaashey 'his cheese' are the same C-11 lexeme under lenition.
caddey (defend family C-20) and dy chaddey "to defend" (C-20) are unmutated and lenited forms of the one verb 'defend/protect' (cf. caddit "defended, protected").
chaghlaa v. 'did change' is the lenited past of caghlaa 'change' in the same family C-26 as caghlaa s.m. 'change, diversity, alteration' (the verbal noun of the same word).
cah s. "battle" and chah a. d. "of battle" is its mutated genitive form, both family C-28.
camm.a is the adjective 'crooked' (C-37), but chamm.v is 'did bend', past of the verb camm 'bend' (C-38) whose own id camm.v exists; adjective and bend-verb are separate printed entries.
cant s.m. 'an auction' and chant 'did auction' (past of cant v. 'bid at auction') are one root in Cregeen's family C-44.
carnane, printed variant of carn "a heap or pile" (C-53), and yn charnane "the heap, &c" (C-53) are radical and lenited forms of the same noun.

carr.v is the printed carr v. 'twist, twine, warp' (C-48), but charr.n is 'yn charr' = 'the tune' (C-55), the lenited form of the noun carr 'a tune'; twist-verb and tune-noun are different lexemes, so charr belongs with carr.n.

cast.x is the pos-less printed cast, a variant of carit "twisted" (from cas "twist", C-48), while chast.v is "did quell or conquer", the mutated past of the different verb cast v. "quell, defeat" (C-74, proper target cast.v).
cayrn.n is 'a trumpet, a horn to blow, a bugle' s.m. (C-81), but chayrn.v is 'did blow the trumpet', past of the verb cayrn 'blow or sound the trumpet' whose own id cayrn.v exists.
yn chappagh 'the captive' (pl. yn chappee) and dy chappee 'of captives' are one captive lexeme in family C-45.
çheet "coming" (v., C-96) and er-jeet "hath, &c. come or arrived" (pt., C-96) are the verb 'come' and its perfect participle, one paradigm.
'yn chere' = 'the comb' is the lenited noun kere s.f. 'a comb, wax' and kere v. 'comb' is the same word verbed, both family K-50 with matching sense (kere.n would be the exact-class target).

chiaull.n is "yn chiaull" s. "the clamour, noise; music", the mutated NOUN kiaull "clamour, noise, din" (proper target kiaull.n), while kiaull.v is the verb entry "make clamour or noise" (both K-82 but different entries).

chionn.a is çhionn a. 'tight, fast, strait, speedy' (C-117), but kionn.v is 'buy, purchase' (K-93, whose past is chionn 'did buy'); tight-adjective and buy-verb are unrelated lexemes sharing only the mutated form.

chionnit.x keys the printed çhionnit pt. (C-117, s'çhionnit 'how tightened or straitened', from çhionn 'tight'); kionn v. (K-93) is 'buy, purchase' - tightened vs buy, the surface collision with kionnit 'bought' misled the note.
dy chleaee "to harrow" and chleiee "did harrow" (both C-145) are lenited forms of the one harrow verb cleaiee/cleiee.
chleayn v. 'did allure, incline, or entice' is the lenited past of cleayn 'entice' (C-147), the same word as cleayn s.m. 'enticement, allurement' in the same family.
chleiee v. "did harrow" and the pos-less cleiee entry, printed variant of cleaiee v. "harrow", are the same verb in family C-145.
Both are C-154: clein s.m. 'the clan, the surname' and dy chlein a. 'of surname', its genitive; the other printed clein (C-145 'harrows', see cleaiyn) is not involved.

The printed chlein entry is a cross-reference 'See chleayn' = 'did allure, incline, or entice' (C-147 entice family); clein.n is 'the clan, the surname' (C-154) - entice vs clan (the note's 'harrows' is yet another clein, C-145).

chleiy.n is yn chleiy "the hedge" (lenited cleigh s.m., C-153), not "dug/dig" as the note claims; the printed bare cleiy is a variant headword under BOTH cleigh "a hedge" (s.m.) and cleigh "dig, delve, quarry" (v.), and cleiy.x is absent from cregeen.tsv, so the print cannot settle which cleiy entry the id names (hedge reading = same, dig reading = different lexeme).
'dy chleiy' = 'to dig, delve' (C-153) is the lenited form of cleiy, printed as a variant of cleigh whose verb entry 'dig, delve, quarry' is in the same family C-153.

chliaghtey.n is "yn chliaghtey" s. "the custom, habit, or practice", the mutated NOUN cliaghtey s. m. "practice, habit, custom, fashion" (proper target cliaghtey.n), while cliaghtey.v is the separate verb entry (C-161).
Both are the C-170 chase verb: dy chloghey 'to chase' and cloghey v. 'chasing' (printed variant of clo 'chase'); no bait lexeme exists in the print.
chloie 'did play or boil' and cloie 'a play' / v. 'play, boil' are one C-173 family under lenition.
yn chlooie "the small feathers" and clooie "small feathers, fur" (s.f., both C-176) are lenited and radical forms of the same noun.
chluin 'didst thou hear' is the lenited form of cluin, a printed variant of cluinn v. 'hear', all in family C-144.
choamr v. "did clothe" is the mutated past of coamr/coamree v. "clothe, dress", both family C-185.
choar.n is 'yn choar' the twister (C-188, radical coar s.f. 'a twister'), but coar.a is the adjective 'agreeable, sociable, civil, indulgent' (C-187); two distinct printed coar lexemes.
yn choardail 'the agreement' and coardail v./s.m. 'an agreement' are one C-189 lexeme.
choayr.n is yn choayr "the bittern" (bird noun, family C-194), but coayr.a is the adjective coayr "odd" (Num. iii. 48, family C-193); two unrelated lexemes.
chombaas 'did encompass' is the lenited past of combaas v. 'compass, surround, encircle', and printed combaase is its variant spelling (also s.m. 'a compass, circular route'), all family C-212.
chood.v is chood v. "did cover", past of the verb cood "cover" (C-232), while coodagh.n is the NOUN coodagh s. m. "a covering"; verb and derived noun are different entries/lexemes.
Both are the C-232 cover verb: chood 'did cover' and coodee.x carries the cha good/cha goodee 'not cover' negative forms of the same verb.
choodee a.d. 'of a cover or covering' and coodee.x (cha good 'not cover', forms of cood v. 'cover') both belong to the C-232 cover family.
my chooidsave "if vouchsafe" (C-235) is the lenited form under my of the single cooidsave 'vouchsafe' lexeme of family C-235 (radical cooidsave a., s'gooidsave "more or most vouchsafe").
chooilleen 'did fulfil, perform, reward, compensate' is the lenited past of cooilleen (C-238), whose noun entry 'recompence, compensation' is the same word's verbal noun in the same family.

chooilleeney.n is "e chooilleeney" s. "his fulfilment, his revenge", the mutated NOUN cooilleeney s. m. "fulfilment, revenge" (proper target cooilleeney.n), while cooilleeney.v is the verb entry "fulfilling, performing, recompensing" (C-238).
Both ids name the printed dy-chooilley / dy chooilley 'every' (D-122 and O-64); chooilley.x just treats dy as particle.

Both are family C-239 remember: chooin 'did remember or recollect' and cooin s., radical of the s'cooin-lhiam 'I remember' group (the note's 'help' gloss is the separate C-246 cooin, which neither id keys).
choon.v is choon "did help, aid, assist" (preterite of coon v. 'help', family C-246), but coon.a is coon "narrow, not wide" (a., family C-245); help verb conflated with the narrow adjective.

chooney.n is 'yn chooney' = 'the help, aid, assistance' (C-246, lenition of cooney s.m. 'help'), but cooney.a is the printed cooney a. pl. 'narrow, strait' (C-245, plural of coon); help-noun and narrow-adjective are unrelated lexemes.
dy choonrey v. "to exchange, barter" is the lenited infinitive of the pos-less coonrey verb stub (printed "coonrey, v."), both family C-248 (the noun "an exchange" is separately coonrey.n).
Both are the C-249 count family: dy choontey 'to reckon, account, cypher' and coontey the pos-less verbal-noun entry ('an account, reckoning' is the same word) under coont 'count'.
ny chooyl pre. 'behind, aback' and cooyl s. 'back' (e chooyl 'his back part', cooyl adv. 'behind, aback') are one C-251 word.
corvaal "confusion, chaos" (s.f.) and yn chorvaal "the confusion, chaos" (both C-268) are radical and lenited forms of the same noun.
chosn 'did gain or gained, did profit or earn' is the lenited past in family C-271 (cosney 'gain'), and printed cosne is a bare entry in the same C-271 family with variant chosne.

chowree.n is "yn chowree" "the sowins" (cowree s. f. "sowins, flummery", C-281, proper target cowree.n), while cowree.a is cowree a. d. "of a mark or marks, or signifying", the genitive of cowrey "mark" (C-280).
Both are C-284: choyrl 'did advise or counsel' and coyrlee, Cregeen's printed variant of coyrl 'advise, counsel, persuade'.
choyrlee and coyrlee are both printed a.d. 'of advice or counsel' plus coyrl/coyrlee variants, all family C-284 - a straight lenition pair.

chraid.v is chraid "did mock, deride" (preterite of the separate craid v. "mock, scoff" entry, id craid.v), but craid.n is the noun craid "mockery, scoffery, irony" (s.f.); verb form attached to the noun entry.

chramp.n is 'yn chramp' = 'the plague' (C-295, lenition of cramp s.m. 'plague'), but cramp.a is the printed cramp a. 'intricate, complicated' (C-294); plague-noun and intricate-adjective are different lexemes.
chred v. "did believe" is the mutated past of cred v. "believe, give credit", with creid its printed pos-less variant, all family C-313.

chred.v is 'did believe or believed' (C-313, past of cred 'believe, give credit'), but kred.n is 'a grunt, a hem, the act of discharging the breath with force' s.m. (K-105), whose mutated form is 'yn chred'; 'creed' is a hallucination.
chreear 'did sift or sifted' and creear 'a sieve, searce' / v. 'sift' are one C-315 family.

chreen.v is chreen "did ripen, &c." (preterite of the separate creen v. "wither, ripen" entry, id creen.v), but creen.a is the adjective creen "ripe, withered"; verb form attached to the adjective entry.

Printed chreogh is a variant of chreoï v. 'did harden' (lenited past of creoi v. 'make hard or harden') and creoï a. is 'hard, obdurate', both family C-323 of the same root word creoi; note's 'spelling variant' rationale is wrong but the entries share one root and sense (verb-past vs adjective conversion).
e chrink/e chroink s. pl. "his hills" and croink "hills, mounts" (variant of crink) are both the plural of cronk "a hill", family C-345.
chront.v is 'did knot' (C-350), past of the verb cront 'knot' whose own id cront.v exists; cront.n is the noun 'a knot'; 'predicament' appears nowhere in either entry.
chroo 'did create, created' and croo s. 'creation' are one C-351 family (the separate croo 'crawling in grubs, maggots' C-352 is not involved).

chrou.n is yn chrou "the horse-shoe; the iron circle of a wheel" (noun, C-357), but crow.v is the verb crow "hover" (C-360, inflections crowagh/crowee match the id); horseshoe noun conflated with the hover verb.

chrow.n is 'yn chrow' = 'the bunch or bush of shrub growing on one stem' (C-359, lenition of crouw s.f.; a second yn chrow is variant of yn chrou 'the horse-shoe' C-357), but crow.v is the printed crow v. 'hover' (C-360); bush/horseshoe nouns and hover-verb are different lexemes.

chroym.x is the printed variant of chroymm v. "did stoop or bow", past of the verb croymm "bow, bend, stoop" (proper target croymm.v), while croym.a is the ADJECTIVE croym "stooped/bent" (cf. s'croym "how stooped or bent forward"), both C-361 but different entries.
Both are the C-365 stem: er chruinnaght 'hath besieged' is er + lenited cruinnaght, and cruinnaght is the printed variant of cruinagh s. 'the close multitude'; same verbal-noun lexeme.
yn chruisht 'the pitcher or pail' and cruishtin (printed variant of cruisht) are one C-367 word.

chryss.v is chryss "did gird or bind with belt, tape, or girdle" (preterite of the separate cryss v. "gird" entry, id cryss.v), but cryss.n is the noun cryss "belt, tape, inkle, girdle" (s.f.); verb form attached to the noun entry.

Both ids span the same three-entry homonym set: the three 'yn chullee' entries ('the colour' C-386, 'the aspect' C-387, 'the tackle' C-388) are exactly the lenited counterparts of the three cullee entries ('a colour or banner', 'the aspect of the air', 'the tackle, furniture, or apparatus') that cullee.n's senses cover.

chummal.n is "yn chummal" s. "the holding or dwelling", the mutated NOUN cummal s. m. "a dwelling, a holding" (proper target cummal.n), while cummal.v is the verb entry "holding, dwelling, inhabiting" (C-390).
Both are C-400 (curm 'charge or duty; enjoin'): er churmal 'hath charged' is er + lenited curmal, the printed variant of curmaghey 'charging, enjoining'.
e churrym 'his duty, his charge' and currym s.m. 'duty, charge' are one C-400 lexeme.
dy hymsagh "to gather together, to accumulate" and hymsee, variant of hyms "did gather, gathered" (both C-128), are lenited forms of the one gather verb (chymsaghey).
chyrmee.x covers hyrm 'did dry, dried' and its variant hyrmee, and hyrmagh.v is 'dy hyrmagh' = 'to dry' (variant dy hyrmaghey), all lenited forms of the same 'dry' verb in family C-130.
cleaiee.v is the verb "harrow" (C-145), while cleiee.a is cleiee a. d. "of hedge or hedges", the genitive of cleigh "hedge" (C-153); the note's gloss-glue is a spurious spelling collision.
cleaiee.v is the verb 'harrow' (C-145, variant cleiee), but cleiee.n is the printed cleiee s. pl. 'hedges' (C-153); harrow-verb and hedges-noun are different lexemes.

cleragh s.m. 'a clerk' (pl. cleree) and cleree a.d. 'of a clerk or clerks' are one C-156 lexeme (a homograph cleragh 'piece in the chimb of a wooden vessel' C-157 also feeds cleragh.n but the clerk link is genuine).
clo "chase, chasing" (v., C-170) lists cloit as its participle, and the bare cloit pt. entry sits in the same chase family C-170; one verb and its participle.
coadeyder s.m. 'a protector' (C-182) and fer choadee are printed as an explicit variant relation within the one C-182 entry, exactly as the note says.
coair.x is coair adv. "near, nigh" (C-184), while coayr.a is coayr a. "odd" (C-193, Num. iii. 48), whose printed variant spelling coair belongs to "odd", not "near".
connysson is Cregeen's printed variant of connaasagh (C-221 'taunting, scoffing, disdainfully sneering'; also a. and s.m. entries in the same family).
connysson is printed as a variant of connaasagh 'taunting, scoffing' and connaasagh.n is 'a disdainful, teasing, gibing person' - one C-221 family.

coodagh.n is the noun coodagh "a covering" (s.m., C-232), but coodee.x is the printed cha goodee entry, variant of cha good "not cover" (negative of the verb cood "cover", C-232); a verb form of 'cover' attached to the noun 'a covering'.

cooish s.f. 'a cause, case, affair' (C-242), but gooish.x is "ny 'gooish" p.p. 'without him or it' (F-83, an elided form of fegooish 'without'), not a nyn-eclipsis of cooish; noun 'affair' and prepositional pronoun 'without him' are different lexemes.

coonlagh.n is s. f. "straw" (C-247, whose real eclipsed form "nyn goonlagh" already feeds it), while goonlagh.v is the separate entry goonlagh v. "abluting washing" (family O-68, the g-prefixed form of oonlaghey "wash").

corrag.x names the pos-less corrag entry that is Cregeen's printed variant of currag 'a bundle of osiers' (C-404); the separate corrag s.f. 'a hand in contempt, a knob' (C-261) keeps its own id corrag.n.
craideyder 'a mocker, scoffer' and craidoilagh (printed as its variant, also a. 'in a scoffing, mocking manner') are one C-289 family.
creid is a printed variant of cred "believe, give credit" (v., C-313); same believe verb.

cum.x is cum/cumm v. 'hold, keep, retain, sustain' (C-390), but cummee.a spans two printed a.d. entries, 'of holding' (C-390) and 'of form or shape' (C-393, from cummey 'shape'), so the blanket merge conflates the shape lexeme with the hold verb.
daa a. "two, the dual number" and "e ghaa" s. "his two" is the same numeral mutated after the possessive, both family D-2.
doo.a is 'black, dark' (D-62), but ghoo.n is 'e ghoo' his word, his fame (G-121, lenited goo 'word'); the black lexeme's lenited entry is ghoo v. 'did blacken', not this noun.

dooys (D-1) is 'give me, or give to me. The em. of dou' - the emphatic prepositional pronoun 'to me' - while doo.v is the verb 'blacken, darken' (D-62) whose future dooys merely collides; the note's 'place-name compounds' is fiction.
doo.v is the verb doo "blacken, darken" (D-62, preterite ghoo "did blacken"), but ghoo.n is e ghoo "his word, his fame" (lenited goo 'word', family G-121); blacken verb conflated with the word noun.
nyn dorçhagh 'your torment' (eclipsed torçhagh noun) and cha dorçhee/cha dorçh 'not torment' (eclipsed torçh verb) are both family T-119, the same 'torment' word as noun and verb.
dorraghys s. m. "darkness" with dorrid its printed variant, and dorrid.x fed by "dy ghorrid/dy ghorraghys" "of darkness", all family D-77.
Both are D-91 'the back': dreeym (printed variant of dreem) and e ghreeym 'his back', its lenited possessive form.

driaght is 'chain' (D-95: driaght v. 'chain', driagh/driaght s., with e ghriaght 'his chain' feeding driaght.n); ghriaght.n keys the G-section e ghriaght 'his group, or drove' (G-156, lenited griaght 'drove') - chain vs drove.
drogh-yantys is a printed variant of drogh-yannoo "evil doings" (s.m., families D-102/J-19); same noun.

The printed druight at G-171 is a bare variant cross-reference under gruight (the family of 'yn ghruight' = 'the measles'), which is what class-x druight.x names, distinct from druight.n s.m. 'dew' (D-111) which has its own id.
eadagh.v (geadagh/dy eadagh v. "jealous, being jealous / to be jealous") and eadee.x (ead v. "be jealous" with variant eadee) are the same verb family E-4.
idd a.d. 'of a hat or hats' (E-26) and 'of a nest or nests' (E-27) is the genitive of edd 'a hat'/'a nest'; the ids collide over the same two families on both sides.

The printed eill v. entry (E-55) is 'arm, fit with armour or arms' (the eilley 'armour' verb); feill (F-86) is 'flesh, butcher's meat' - the lenited flesh forms (dty eill) already map into feill.n, but the eill.v entry is the armour verb, not flesh.

endeilagh.n is dty endeilagh "thy defender" (noun, F-94), which belongs with the separate fendeilagh s.m. "a defender" entry (id fendeilagh.n), not with fendeilagh.a, the distinct bare adjective entry in the family.

enm v. 'name' (E-74), but enmys.n names the printed enmys s.m. 'as much as that it could be named, a little more than nothing', a lexicalized quantity noun; the matching verb entry is enmys v. 'name' (id enmys.v, a separate seed row), so this pair links the wrong enmys entry.

enn.v is Cregeen's enn v. "feel" (E-69, whose paradigm ennym/ennys feeds the id), while enney.n is enney s. m. "knowledge, as respects knowing one person from another" (E-73); the E-73 variant "enn, v. s. to know" already folds into enney.n, so the entries gloss different lexemes.
Both are F-93 'ask': my en / my enys 'if ask or enquire' is the f-dropped lenited form of fen 'ask, enquire'.
er-egin is printed as a variant of er-eigin 'on force' (E-46/E-77) - one 'by force' word.

foddee.x is the adv. entry foddee "may be, perhaps, peradventure" (F-148), the impersonal use of the same modal fod whose verb entry foddee "may or might, can or could" sits in the same family, and Cregeen's own note ties the adv. example back to foddee v.
fod is a printed variant of fodd v. 'may, can' (F-148) and foddagh v. 'might, could' (with dy voddagh 'that could') is the conditional of the same modal in the same family.

gannidys.n is the noun "mockery, scorn, derision", while ghannidys.v is the "e ghannidys" v. entry "his despising, scorning", the possessed form of the separate printed gannidys v. entry (proper target gannidys.v, which exists as its own id).
gard.n is the noun 'guard' s.m. (G-20), but ghard.v is 'cha ghard' did or didst not guard, negative past of the verb gard 'guard' whose own id gard.v exists.

gheill 'did spring' (G-48) is the lenited past of geill v. 'spring', and geill.n hosts the matching geill s.m. 'a spring of water' (G-48); note geill.n also hosts the homograph 'heed, notice' (G-49), and the note's 'Gell surname' gloss is baseless.
geinnagh "sand" (s.f., G-50) lists geinnee as its plural/genitive, and geinnee "of sand" (a. d., G-50) is that genitive of the same noun.

geir s. belongs to family G-187 (geyre 'sharp/sour': dy gheir 'of smart or pain', bainney geir 'sour milk'), but gheir.v is the printed gheir v. 'did crow' (G-52, lenited past of geirr 'crow'); sour/pain noun and crow-verb are unrelated lexemes.

gerjagh.n is the NOUN gerjagh s. m. "comfort, consolation, happiness", while gerjee.x is the VERB gerj/gerjee "comfort, console" (G-53); the verb's conditional inflection gerjagh merely collides with the noun's spelling.
Both are the G-53 comfort family: gerjee (pos-less entries beside gerj v. 'comfort, console') and gherjee 'did comfort, comforted'.
gerrit is printed as a variant of gerrid (G-63) and yn gherrid is 'the short time' - one 'short/brevity' word.
ghiar "did cut. See yiare" (G-62) is the lenited preterite of giar "cut" (v.); same cut verb.

ghiar is printed as 'did cut. See yiare' (G-62, lenited past of the cut verb), but giare.a is giare a. 'short, momentary, brief' (G-63); the cut verb and the short adjective are different families and different lexemes.
ghiarrey.a is a. pl. "short", the mutated plural of giare "short" (G-63, proper target giarrey.a "short" a. pl.), while giarrey.v is the verb "cutting, hewing" (G-62).
Both are G-114 forms of gob 'mouth/beak': gib 'beaks' (s. pl.) / 'of mouths in contempt' and e ghib 'of his mouth' (see gob); same plural/genitive stem.
ghioot 'did gift, gifted' and gioot 'a gift' / v. are one G-75 family under lenition.

ghlass.v is ghlass "did lock, or make sure" (preterite of glass v. "lock or make sure", family G-85), but glass.a is the adjective glass "pale, gray, pale blue; green, verdant" (G-84); lock verb conflated with the colour adjective.

ghlassey.v is 'dy ghlassey' = 'to embrace, to lock' (G-85, from glass 'a lock'), but glassey.a is glassey a. pl. 'pale, gray, green' (G-84, plural of glass the colour); lock-verb and colour-adjective are different lexemes.

ghlenney.v is "er ghlenney" "hath cleansed", the perfect of the verb glenney "cleansing" (proper target glenney.v, which exists), while glenney.a is a. pl. "clean, clear, pure, perfect", the plural of the adjective glen (both G-90 but different entries).
ghlioon.v is 'did kneel' (G-97), past of the verb glioon 'kneel' whose own id glioon.v exists; glioon.n is the noun 'a knee, a crooked timber'.
ghloyr 'did glorify' and gloyr 'glory' / v. 'glorify' are one G-105 family.
goin "I would take" (from gow-in) and ghoin "I would take" (from ghowin, lenited) are both conditional 1sg of 'take' in family G-135.

'yn ghortagh' = 'the hurt' and gortagh v. 'hurting' are both family G-129, the same 'hurt' word as noun and verb (the note's 'stingy' gloss belongs to the unrelated gortagh a. G-131, but the id pair itself is same-word).
both printed entries ("my ghowys" v. and the gowys stub) are cross-references to goys "shall or will take or receive", future of gow "take", family G-135.

The printed ghrain entry is a variant of ghrainn 'did grave or carve' (G-138, radical grainn 'grave, carve'), but grain.n is 'oat-grist' s.m. (G-137); carving-verb and grist-noun are different lexemes.
ghrainn 'did grave or carve' and grainnee (printed variant of grainn) are one G-138 engrave family.
grainnee is a printed variant of grainn "grave, carve" (v., G-138) and ghrainnee "did, &c. grave" (G-138) is its lenited preterite; one engrave verb.
ghrees v. 'did stir up to action, or kindle to wrath' (lenited past) and greesee (printed variant of grees) are both family G-151, the same incite verb.

ghreim.v is ghreim v. "did hold, grasp, stitch" (the mutated verb), while ghreme.x is "e ghreme/e ghreim" s. "his hold, grasp, stitch, or bite", the possessed NOUN greim "a bite, hold" (proper target greim.n), both G-153 but different entries.

Both are G-153: ghreim 'did hold, grasp, stitch' is the past of greimm 'bite, hold', which Cregeen prints as a variant of greim 'a bite, hold, stitch' and whose forms all feed greim.n (no greim.v exists).
ghreinn 'did urge or stimulate, did encourage' and greinnee are both family G-154 (greinn 'urge/incite').
e ghreme is a printed variant of e ghreim "his hold, grasp, stitch, or bite", lenited form of greim "a bite, hold, stitch, gobbet, or bit" (s.m., G-153); same noun.
'yn ghrynder' = 'the giber' and grynder (printed see-reference to grinder s.m. 'a satirist, a taunter') are both family G-161, the same word.
e ghweeaghyn s. "his cursing" is the possessive-mutated form of gweeaghyn v. "cursing" (G-186); no separate noun radical is printed, so both entries gloss the one verbal noun "cursing".
Both are G-69 'conceive': gientyn 'conceiving' and er ny yientyn 'having been conceived', its mutated participial construction.

gimman s. (G-73) is the radical of ghimman 'an admirer, a suiter or lover' (Ezk. xvi. 33); imman.v is 'drive' (I-12), and the participial gimman 'driving' entry in I-12 already feeds imman.v - lover vs drive.

gione.x is my ny gione "about them, about whom" (p. p., family M-171, the mychione 'about' preposition-pronoun), but kione.n is the noun kione 'head' (s.m., with yn chione/nyn gione); a preposition entry conflated with the head noun, the hug-type failure.

There is no printed haaue headword: printed h-aaue forms divide across three radicals, e haaue 'his saw' (S-3, saaue), my haaue 'my safety' (S-19, saue), and ny haaue 'idle' (T-5, taau); taaue.x is the T-5 'idle' variant entry, so the equivalence holds only if haaue.n names the ny haaue/taau reading, which the print does not settle.
dy hannaght "to continue, abide, tarry, or endure" is the lenited infinitive of tannaght v. "continuing, tarrying, abiding", both family T-18.

hast.x names the pos-less printed hast entry 'see hiast' (S-100, shast/shiast 'dry, sterile, barren, not giving milk'), but tast.v is 'heed, attend, notice, observe' (T-31), whose past hast 'did heed' has its own id hast.v.
The printed hig entry sits in the C-96 come family (radicalInitial Ch, i.e. çheet) alongside tar 'come, come away'; hig is the future 'will come' of that suppletive verb.
hoil, printed variant of hoill "did deserve, merit, earn" (T-111), is the lenited preterite of toill "deserve" (v., T-111); same verb.
howse is a printed variant of howsh 'did measure, measured' (T-125), the lenited past of towse, and towse.n is towse s.m. 'a measure' (with towse v. 'measuring') in the same family T-125.

jean.v is the irregular verb "do/make" (whose real future nee, J-19 "will or wilt do", already feeds jean.v as a closed-class form), while nee.x is the B-65 COPULA entry (the pos-less nee stub alongside "cha nee" "is not" and "dy nee" "that is, that were, that was") - the cur/hug failure mode.

jeeg.x is the pos-less jeeg entry, Cregeen's printed variant of the noun jeeig s.f. 'a ditch, a moat, or drain' (whose id jeeig.n exists), but jeeig.v is the separate verb entry 'drain, ditch' (both J-30).

The printed yeih entry (J-44) is a cross-reference 'See ny yeih' = ny-yeih adv. 'nevertheless, notwithstanding, howbeit' in the jeï 'after/behind' family; jeih.a is the numeral 'ten' (J-47) - nevertheless vs ten.

yeih.x is the bare yeih entry (J-44), a see-reference to ny-yeih "nevertheless, notwithstanding, howbeit" in the yeï 'after' family, but jeih.n is the numeral jeih "ten" (J-47, e yeih "his ten"); 'nevertheless' conflated with 'ten'.
keynnagh s.f. 'moss' (pl. keynnee) and keynnee a.d. 'of moss' are both family K-65, the genitive/attributive form of the same noun.
lhiannoo s. m. "a child" and lhiennoo a. d. "of children, of the child" is its genitive/plural-stem form, both family L-72.

lhiannoo.n is 'a child' (L-72, plural lhiennoo feeds it), but lhiennoo.v is the printed '<dy> lhiennoo' v. 'did surname, surnamed' (S-246, Mark iii. 16-17); child-noun and surname-verb are different lexemes.
varroo.v is dy my varroo 'to kill or slay me' (lenited marroo v. 'killing') and marroo.n is marroo s. / yn varroo 'the dead or deceased person' - both Cregeen's one marroo kill/dead family M-32.

share "better, best" (a., M-91) is printed as "the comp. and sup. of mie" (relation compSupOf mie), and mie.v is the closed-class id whose sole form is that same irregular comparative share of mie "good"; one suppletive paradigm.

mooar.v names the printed mooar v. 'grudge, envy, seeing big or large' (M-132), but smoo a. 'bigger, biggest' is printed with an explicit CompSupVariant relation to the adjective mooar 'big, large, great'; smoo belongs to mooar.a, not the grudge verb.

mooin.n is mooin s. "back" (M-136, "er e vooin" on his back), while vooin.x is fed by wooin p. p. "from us" (V-3), a prepositional pronoun; neither is the other's mutation (the urine verb is separately mooin.v).
ollay.n is 'a swan' (O-46; its plural ollee is only an inflected form inside that entry), but the printed ollee a.d. entry that ollee.a names is 'of cattle' (O-43, genitive of ollagh 'cattle').
rio v. 'freeze, coagulate', rio s.m. 'frost, ice', and rioee a.d. 'of frost or ice' are one R-85 family.

sahll.n is sahll "saim... the blubber of fish... grease" (s.m., S-7, with saill as its printed variant), but saill.v is the separate verb entry saill "salt" (v., S-10, inflections saillagh/saillym); the note's "identical fat/blubber definition" only holds for the S-7 variant, not the salt verb the id names.
sannish s.f. 'a whisper' and sonnish (printed as variant of sannish for both the noun and the verb 'to whisper or susurrate') are one word in family S-14.

sayntoilagh.n is the s. m. entry "a covetous person" (person-noun), while sayntoilee.a is the printed sayntoilee a. entry, the idem/comparative of the ADJECTIVE sayntoilagh "covetous" (proper target sayntoilagh.a), both S-23 but different entries.

seigh s.m. 'a mix or stir' (S-76, 'pup of the first litter' example) is the action noun of the printed seiy v. 'mix, stir' in the same family; caveat: the seiy.v id also spans the homographic seiy 'to push or shove' (S-75).
sharragh s.m. 'a foal' (pl. sharree) and sharree a.d. (its genitive) are one S-94 word.

sheillee.a is sheillee "of salix or willow" (a. d., S-126, see sheillagh "salix, black willow or sally"), but shellagh.x is the printed shellagh entry of S-128, a variant of shell "imagine, suppose, conjecture" (v.); willow adjective conflated with the imagine verb.
soi v. 'set, sit, plant' (S-307) and soiaghey (printed as variant of soiagh v. 'setting, planting', its verbal noun) are the same verb in family S-307.
soi v. "set, sit, plant" and soie (printed pos-less variant, plus soie v. "sit, set, plant") are the same verb, family S-307.

Both are the S-312 stem: soilshagh 'enlightening, declaring, publishing' is the verbal noun of soilsh 'enlighten, declare, illume', and soilshee is Cregeen's printed variant of that verb (hoilshee a.d. 'of light or enlightening'); the table folds the soilsh verb under soilshee.a.
taa is printed as a variant of taah 'a weld, a solder' / v. 'weld, solder' - one T-1 word.

tastey "notice, heed, observation" and tastid "sagacity, attention" are separate printed headwords (distinct -ey/-id derivatives, both s.m., T-31), yet the family apparatus marks e hastid as a variant of e hastey "his intellect, sagacity, heed, notice"; the print does not settle whether they are one lexeme or two.
Printed thollee is an explicit variant relation to toallee a. 'tall and strong, robust, athletic, corpulent' (T-104), with ro hollee 'See hoallee' in the same family, exactly as the note says.

toiggaltagh is printed only as a bare pos-less variant of toiggalagh between the s. m. entry "a person that understands" (= toiggalagh.n) and the comparative s'toiggaltagh a. "how knowing"; the print never says whether the variant names the person-noun or the adjective (the id's comp/sup forms s'toiggaltagh/s'toiggaltee suggest the adjective toiggalagh.a).
Both are T-124: towl 'a hole' with plural tuill 'holes', and the tuill a.d. entry is that noun's genitive in the same family.
yllagh s.m. 'a call or shout' and yllee.x (yll/yllee shout-verb variants) are one Y-12 family.
dy yllagh "to call, to shout or cry out" and yllee, printed variant of yll "shout, cry out, exclaim, call" (v., Y-12), are forms of the one shout verb.
ymmilt v. 'tumble or roll, as a horse does after work' and ymmylt s. 'wallowing' (2 Pet. ii. 22, with printed see/variant relations to ymmilt) are the same word in family Y-15.
ymmilt v. "tumble or roll, as a horse does after work" and ymmylt, printed only as see/variant cross-references to ymmilt (plus the same word's s. "wallowing"), are one lexeme, family Y-15.
Both are Y-23: yns 'learn, teach, instruct' and ynsagh s.m. 'learning, literature, erudition, instruction, doctrine', its verbal/action noun (also listed as an inflected form of yns).
yns v. 'learn, teach, instruct' and ynsee a.d. 'of learning or teaching' are one Y-23 word.
